name: What is the difference between gunite, shotcrete, and fiberglass pools?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between gunite, shotcrete, and fiberglass when choosing a custom pool for a luxury Los Angeles home?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between gunite, shotcrete, and fiberglass when choosing a custom pool for a luxury Los Angeles home?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common decision point for custom pool buyers is whether they want a true custom concrete pool or a preformed fiberglass shell. Gunite and shotcrete are both concrete-based methods used to create a shell that can be shaped to fit the yard, architecture, and design goals. Fiberglass pools are faster to install, but they come in fixed sizes and shapes, which limits customization. For luxury homes in Los Angeles, concrete usually makes more sense when the project needs a specific geometry, integrated spa, sun shelf, negative-edge look, or custom finish. The tradeoff is longer build time and more variables during construction. Fiberglass can be attractive for buyers who want a simpler, faster install and lower design complexity, but it is not the best fit for every site. A strong comparison page should focus on decision criteria: shape flexibility, finish options, installation speed, maintenance expectations, access constraints, and budget. Searchers often want a direct recommendation, not just definitions. The best answer is that concrete is the most flexible option for bespoke design, while fiberglass is the more standardized alternative.
acceptedAnswer.description: Gunite and shotcrete are concrete pool shell methods that allow custom shapes, sizes, and finishes. Fiberglass pools arrive as prefabricated shells and install faster, but they offer fewer design options. For high-end Los Angeles projects, concrete is usually preferred when the goal is a fully custom layout and integrated outdoor design.
